notes: All coordinates are sample-1x px (448x288, 16px cells, cell (cx,cy)). F.sample() re-rendered from the module is byte-identical to r6/sample-1x.png. Of the r5 defects: the corner-picker defect (SW4 two cells apart) is fixed, the NW base shard is now a flat lying piece, and the hole's west wall reads acceptably. Lip, dimming, seams and kerb all hold. The repeat defect is not gone. The straight edges still show a lattice-locked recurrence above the advisory threshold. Separately, the corner/stair diagonals are a pure deterministic 4-cycle: there is no hash, so every long diagonal has an exact 64px x 64px period. The object-gate PASS is advisory (uncalibrated profile) and is not a human allow. Crops and test renders are in /tmp/vqa-r6/ (diamond-1x.png = 40x26 diamond test shape, n13n3_pairs.png).

ragged_ruin_edge.evidence: The N edge (north-edge-4x) shows flat, low slabs at uneven depths, with missing corners and loose pieces lying on the earth. There is no picket/comb silhouette and chips are scattered, not in a dotted row. The S edge and diagonals are similar. Convex corner variants now drop whole slabs; NW/NE/SW/SE rows in edge-tiles-8x have no lone triangle shards.

no_kerb.evidence: None of the 16x4 straight + 16 corner + iso tiles in edge-tiles-8x has a continuous dressed rim. Beyond the slabs the tile is dirt body plus the lip shadow.

no_square_holes.evidence: The 2x2 hole (cells 9..10,6..7) reads as a rounded pit, with slabs breaking into it and no cell-aligned notches (sample-2x, nw-sw-diagonals-4x). The west wall (E16/E3 at (8,6),(8,7)) is broken enough.

seamless.evidence: `flag_dirt_art.py check` prints OK. Mean luminance step between dirt-dirt pixel pairs is 7.53 across vertical cell borders (n=3710) vs 7.55 at 8px in, and 7.25 across horizontal borders vs 9.76 interior. No border lines or steps.

no_repeat_grid.evidence: Variant dump of the N row y=2, x7..20: NW N13 N3 N5 N11 N13 N3 N7 N10 N15 N2 N8 N11 NE. S row y=14, x9..25: SW2 S8 S10 S15 S2 S5 S11 S16 S S7 S10 S14 S2 S6 S10 S13 SE2. No identical tile within 3 cells (Chebyshev) anywhere in the sample (0 pairs), and all 63 edge-variant names/hashes are distinct. However: (1) Straight edges. Because a cell can only match one exactly 4k cells away, every recurrence lands on the 64px lattice. In this sample the two-cell block N13,N3 is pixel-identical (32x16 px) at x8-9 and x12-13, and appears a third time at (20-21,13); N11 repeats at x11 and x19 (128px). Pixel autocorrelation of the N band (y24-48, x128-320): 0.694 at 64px and 0.708 at 128px, vs 0.544-0.61 at other shifts. That is +0.14, against the r5 bar of <=0.05. The author's shift-selfsim shows the same thing (0.58 vs ~0.41). Over a 200x200 test, P(same tile at +4) = 0.249 and P(2-run repeated at +4) = 0.059, which is by design. (2) Diagonals. Worse, and new to this review: the corner picker is (step//2 + 3*(line//6) + salt) mod 4 with no hash. Along one staircase the line is constant, so NW/inNW/SW/... cycle strictly with period 4. The sample already shows NW (7,2)=NW (3,6), SW4 (3,8)=SW4 (7,12), NE (20,2)=NE (24,6), inSW2 (4,8)=inSW2 (8,12). On the 40x26 diamond test, 32x32 blocks around NW corner cells 4 steps apart are 0.754 identical, vs 0.42-0.43 at 1-3 steps. This is a fixed 64px diagonal period, the same failure r5 flagged on straight edges, moved to the stairs. At 4x the long diagonal reads as a regular sawtooth (/tmp/vqa-r6/diamond-nwdiag-4x.png).

beodeul_quality.evidence: Dirt body variants have mean luminance 101.3-104.4 (~102.5). The first non-dirt pixel walking down from the dirt in all 192 N-edge columns is the lip shadow (112,80,46) in 186 of them; its luminance is 85.7, 16.4% darker than the body. N-edge slab tops (y32-44, lum>130) average 174.9 vs body slabs 201.9 (13% dimmer). On board-new-vs-current-2x it sits plausibly next to the temple-ruins court, though the body is brighter and busier (pre-existing).

preexisting_issues: Flag body: the joint grid shows on 16px cell borders, and the triangular facet lattice repeats across the court (visible in sample-2x and diamond tests).
Flag body slab tops are brighter and higher in contrast than the Beodeul temple-ruins stone.
Dirt body pebble pairs and orange clods repeat on a visible regular lattice (diamond-nw-3x).
defects: Corner/stair diagonals are a deterministic 4-cycle (no hash along a staircase). Every long diagonal repeats exactly every 64px x 64px: block identity 0.75 at 4 steps vs 0.42 at 1-3. Visible as a regular sawtooth on long diagonals.

Straight-edge recurrences are locked to the 4-cell lattice. A pixel-identical N13,N3 two-cell block appears at x8-9 and x12-13 on the 14-cell showcase N edge (and again at (20-21,13)), and N11 at x11/x19. N-band autocorrelation is 0.69/0.71 at 64/128px vs ~0.55 baseline, exceeding the +0.05 bar.
fixes: Diagonals: add a per-cell hash, e.g. idx = (step//2 + H(line, step//8, salt)) % 4 or a hashed pick among several variants per phase, and reject a choice equal to the corner tile 1-3 steps back on the same staircase (evaluate those deterministically). Verify on a long diamond: 32px block identity at 4 and 8 steps should be within ~0.05 of the 1-3 step values.

Straight edges: do not tie identity to along mod 4. For example choose from all 16 variants by hash and resolve collisions against the 3 predecessors deterministically, or re-hash the phase offset per 4-cell block (off = H(other, along//4)). That lets equal tiles land at 5, 6 or 7 apart as well, not only at 4k. Verify with N-band autocorrelation: no 32..128px shift more than ~0.05 above the others, and no repeated identical 2-cell runs on the 14-cell sample edge.
